item.title: Rational contractions in quasi-Banach spaces: convergence, multiplicity of fixed points and applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.16170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study self-maps $f$ of a complete $b$-metric space $(U,d)$ (constant $b\ge1$) satisfying the rational contractive condition \[ d(fu,fv)\le\frac{d(u,fv)+d(v,fu)+\kappa}{b\,[d(u,fu)+d(v,fv)]+1}\,d(u,v)\qquad(u,v\in U), \] with $\kappa\in[0,1)$. We first observe that the two-parameter family of conditions studied in our earlier work reduces, after a rescaling of the $b$-metric, to this one-parameter form. We then prove: (A) every Picard sequence converges to a fixed point, with an explicit a~priori estimate whose geometric ratio depends only on $b$, $\kappa$ and $d(u_0,fu_0)$, an a~posteriori estimate, and asymptotic rate at most $\kappa$; (B) a structure theorem: such maps are automatically continuous, every fixed point attracts the whole ball of radius $(1-\kappa)/2$, distinct fixed points are at distance at least $(1-\kappa)/2$ (sharp), basins of attraction are clopen, and the number of fixed points does not exceed the number of connected components of $U$; in particular the fixed point is unique on connected spaces; (C) Ulam--Hyers stability of the fixed-point problem. The class of such maps is not invariant under passing from a quasi-norm to the equivalent $p$-norm metric, so the quasi-Banach results are not formal consequences of the metric ones. A gluing principle shows that the multiplicity permitted by (B) occurs. As applications we obtain existence, exact multiplicity and error estimates for infinite nonlinear systems with relay-type forcing in $\ell^p$, $0<p<1$, and for nonlinear perturbations of Volterra-type equations $f=\pm a+T_gf+\psi(f(z_0))k$ in the Hardy space $H^p$, $0<p<1$, where $T_gf(z)=\int_0^z f(\zeta)g'(\zeta)\,d\zeta$ and $g\in\BMOA$.
item.dc:creator: A. H. Ansari Komachali, Y. U. Gaba, M. Aphane, I. Yildirim

item.title: Meridional ranks of iterated Whitehead doubles
item.description: arXiv:2611.15673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every iterated untwisted Whitehead double of a nontrivial two-bridge knot satisfies the meridional rank conjecture. More precisely, for such a knot $K$ and every $N\geq0$, the augmentation rank, meridional rank, and bridge number of $\operatorname{Wh}^N(K)$ are all $2^{N+1}$. We use microlocal sheaf theory and a doubling construction to produce a lower bound for the meridional rank of the Whitehead double, assuming the peripheral data satisfy suitable conditions. For two-bridge knots, the required curves arise from ideal points detecting nonzero boundary slopes. In contrast, the ordinary group rank of an $N$-fold Whitehead double is at most the rank of the companion group plus $N$. We also give a non-example when the doubling construction does not work -- the first Whitehead double of the square knot has augmentation rank at most 5, whereas its meridional rank and bridge number are 6.
item.dc:creator: Honghao Gao, Shijie Gu, Zhenkun Li, Jian Wang

item.title: Countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit
item.description: arXiv:2611.17315v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit. Given an infinite compact metric countable space $X$, we show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$, the collection of continuous functions on $X$ to itself admitting a dense orbit, is always nonempty. We then classify the systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ up to topological conjugacy in terms of the second Cantor--Bendixson derivative $X^{(2)}$: if $X^{(2)} = \emptyset$ then all systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ are mutually conjugate, while if $X^{(2)} \neq \emptyset$ then $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ contains $2^{\aleph_0}$ pairwise nonconjugate systems. The proof of the latter relies on a gluing construction for countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit, which is of independent interest. We also show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ is nowhere dense in $C(X,X)$ with the compact-open topology. We also study the Ellis semigroup $E(X,f)$ of a countable dynamical system. We characterize, under the assumption that $|\omega(x,f)| = 1$ for each $x \in X^{(1)}$, when the nontrivial functions of $E(X,f)$ are continuous. In particular, for the family constructed on spaces with $|X^{(2)}| \geq 2$, every nontrivial function of the Ellis semigroup is discontinuous.
item.dc:creator: Jhon P\'erez-Remolina, Carlos Uzc\'ategui-Aylwin

item.title: d-Spectral Bitopological Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.26484v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the category of d-spectral spaces, a bitopological analogue of the spectral spaces of Stone and Hochster. A d-spectral space is a bitopological space satisfying three conditions: the join of its two topologies is compact, it is d-sober in the sense of Jung and Moshier, and each of its two topologies is a coherent frame. We establish a dual equivalence between this category and the category of d-lattices satisfying the finitary cut rules. The constructions implementing the duality are the d-lattice of compact open sets of a d-spectral space and the d-spectrum construction for d-lattices. We further show that spectral spaces embed as a full subcategory of d-spectral spaces that is both reflective and coreflective. Finally, the patch space of a d-spectral space is d-Boolean, and its de Groot dual is again d-spectral, mirroring the classical spectral case.
item.dc:creator: Hang Yang, Dexue Zhang

item.title: If the moduli space of metrics is Borel, then it is completely metrizable
item.description: arXiv:2608.16169v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a metrizable space. We prove that the space of compatible metrics on $X$ is Borel in the space of continuous pseudometrics, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence, if and only if $X$ is $\sigma$-compact. These conditions are equivalent to complete metrizability of the space of compatible metrics; the same characterization holds for each component. For ultrametrizable $X$ and $R\subseteq[0,\infty)$ containing $0$ and arbitrarily small positive elements, we prove analogous results for compatible $R$-valued ultrametrics and their $R$-components, {with neighborhoods defined by agreement at every point pair where either ultrametric exceeds a positive $\epsilon\in R$}. For the nonempty subspaces of complete compatible metrics and complete compatible $R$-valued ultrametrics, Borelness and complete metrizability are equivalent to compactness of $X$. The proofs use continuous families of metrics parametrized by trees or subsets of compact completions.
item.dc:creator: Yoshito Ishiki

item.title: Yet another approach to measuring distance in some hyperspaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.00249v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we define a new partial distance on hyperspaces consisting of closed balls, which is a partial metric in the sense of Matthews. We prove that these partial metric spaces are complete if and only if the metric spaces from which the corresponding ball spaces arise are complete. Finally, we compare the topology induced by the new partial distance with that induced by the classical Hausdorff distance.
item.dc:creator: Dariusz Bugajewski, Piotr Ma\'ckowiak

item.title: C*-embeddings of spaces of probability measures, nonnegative measures and unit balls
item.description: arXiv:2611.13857v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a Tychonoff space $X$ and $p\in\{d,\beta,R,\tau,\sigma,a\}$ let $M_p(X)$ be the space of discrete, compactly supported, Radon, $\tau$-additive, $\sigma$-additive or finitely additive signed measures on $X$, regarded as a subspace of $M(\beta X)=C(\beta X)^*$ with the weak$^*$ topology, and let $M^+_p(X)$, $U_p(X)$ and $P_p(X)$ be its subsets of nonnegative measures, measures of norm at most one, and probability measures. In the companion paper it was shown that $M_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M_q(X)$ iff it is $C^*$-embedded iff it is $G_\delta$-dense. We show that $G_\delta$-density of $Q_p(X)$ in $Q_q(X)$ is the same condition for all $Q\in\{M,M^+,U,P\}$, and that $C^*$-embedding of $Q_p(X)$ in $Q_q(X)$ implies $G_\delta$-density, while the converse fails for $Q\in\{M^+,U,P\}$. We prove that $M^+_p(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $M^+(\beta X)$ iff $P_p(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $P(\beta X)$, that pseudocompactness of $P_p(X)$ implies pseudocompactness of all its powers, and that the unit ball $U_R(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $U(\beta X)$ iff $P_R(X)$ is pseudocompact. If $\beta X$ is $\kappa$-metrizable (e.g., a product of metrizable compact spaces or a compact group), then pseudocompactness of $P_p(X)$ and the $C^*$-embeddings of $P_p(X)$, $U_p(X)$ and $M^+_p(X)$ in $P(\beta X)$, $U(\beta X)$ and $M^+(\beta X)$ are equivalent to the $C$-embedding of $M_p(X)$ in $M(\beta X)$. Consequently, $P_\tau(X)$ is pseudocompact for every pseudocompact dense subspace $X$ of a Tychonoff cube. This gives a space $X$ for which $P_\tau(X)$ is pseudocompact while the space $P_R(X)$ of Radon probability measures is not, and answers a question of the first author.
item.dc:creator: E. A. Reznichenko, Yu. V. Sadovnichiy

item.title: Compact totally separated types
item.description: arXiv:2609.10447v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Perhaps surprisingly, there are infinite types that can be exhaustively searched mechanically in finite time. We use ideas from topology to build plenty of them, referring to searchable types as compact types, and we use ordinals to measure their logical complexity. We consider two systems of ordinal notations under which a single notation denotes both a discrete ordinal and a compact one, with an embedding of the former into the latter whose image has empty complement. A boolean valued function decides which points in the image of the embedding are isolated and which are topological limit points. The first system consists of the traditional Brouwer codes and the second is an inductive-recursive universe generalizing them. The discrete ordinals so obtained are trichotomous, and the compact ones have the least element property for complemented subsets, but these two desirable properties cannot be fulfilled simultaneously in a constructive setting. The compact ordinals obtained from Brouwer codes further enjoy a boolean Leibniz principle, which has the notion of total separatedness as its topological counterpart. This extends previous work from G\"odel's system T to intensional Martin-L\"of type theory with univalent universes, and is formalized in Agda in the TypeTopology repository.
item.dc:creator: Mart\'in H\"otzel Escard\'o

item.title: A Stone-Weierstrass Theorem for Polish Spaces, Given by Logic
item.description: arXiv:2611.08901v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Stone-Weierstrass theorem obtains every continuous function on a compact space as a uniform limit of functions built from a separating family by finitely many operations. We extend the theorem to every separable metric space, and in particular to every Polish space, by admitting countable suprema and infima according to weights computed from the construction. For a countable, uniformly bounded separating family whose supremum metric makes the space separable, the functions so built are exactly the bounded Lipschitz functions, and their uniform limits are exactly the bounded uniformly continuous functions. The theorem was discovered, and first proved, in infinitary real-valued logic, where the weights are the a priori bounds of formulas and the uniform approximation is equivalent to an approximate form of Beth's definability theorem, which carries Reggio's correspondence from compact spaces to separable metric spaces. The same bounds draw an exact line between the two forms of definability when the values of the coordinates in the models of the implicit definition form a set separable for the supremum metric: an implicitly defined predicate has an explicit definition precisely when the defining function is Lipschitz, and admits uniform approximation by sentences precisely when that function is uniformly continuous. We also give a purely topological-analytic proof of the theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Iovino
